items.ai_reason: Practical how-to guide on running open-weight models locally with Ollama and LM Studio, including hardware requirements and download sizes. It is useful and accessible but recycles existing facts (Epoch AI's four-month gap analysis from May, the Qwen 3.8-Max comparison) rather than reporting a new development; no in-window release, benchmark, or policy change is announced. Tutorial-grade value, worth knowing but not urgent.
items.ai_summary: A tutorial explaining how to run open-weight AI models locally using free tools like Ollama and LM Studio, noting that the best open models now lag closed frontier models by roughly four months and that small models run on about 8GB of VRAM or Mac unified memory.
items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Open-weight models have trailed the best closed models by an average of four months since January 2026, according to Epoch AI's May 29 analysis.
- Ollama and LM Studio are free, small models need about 8GB of VRAM or Mac unified memory, and LM Studio can operate entirely offline.
- The largest open models, such as Alibaba's 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen 3.8-Max, sit far beyond consumer hardware, and closed models won 24 of 31 tests in Alibaba's own comparison.
Open-weight AI models now trail the best closed models by only about four months on average, and a growing number of them run on hardware you probably already own.
"Open-weight" means the company publishes the weights, the files holding everything the model learned, so anyone can download and run them. Two free programs, Ollama and LM Studio, handle the rest, and Gemma 4 downloads in Ollama's library range from about 4.6GB to 20GB.
With open models, you don't need to pay $20 a month for an AI subscription or send your conversations to someone else's servers to get a capable chatbot. This guide explains how to download and run AI models directly on your computer, what kind of hardware you'll need, and how to get started with free tools like Ollama and LM Studio.
Whether you want to save money, keep your conversations private, or experiment with AI models you can customize yourself, setting up a local AI assistant may be easier than you think.
Why run an AI model on your own machine
A cloud chatbot sends every prompt to a company's servers, and a court ordered OpenAI to preserve ChatGPT logs, including deleted ones, as Decrypt reported in a review of privacy-focused AI tools. A local model keeps the conversation on your computer and nobody can use it without your permission.
LM Studio's documentation says the app "can operate entirely offline, just make sure to get some model files first," and that documents attached to a chat can be used entirely offline too.
Subscriptions to paid chatbots run about $20 per month, while the software here is free. The cost shifts to hardware you may already have.
Licenses decide what you can do with downloaded weights. DeepSeek's R1 series is under the MIT License, and its model card says the models "support commercial use, allow for any modifications and derivative works," while Google's Gemma 4 and OpenAI's gpt-oss ship under Apache 2.0.
Running models on an open-source license like Apache or MIT means you are free to use, modify, and do whatever you want with a model. This means users are able to access improved and modified versions of a specific model that better fit their needs. Maybe you need a model that is good at medicine, so you don’t care about how good it codes. This level of personalization is only available in customized models.
What your hardware can actually run
Models are sized in parameters, the internal numbers adjusted during training, and the download grows with them. The model has to fit in your graphics card's video memory, known as VRAM, or in a Mac's unified memory, which the processor and graphics chip share.
As a general rule, you'll want at least 8GB of VRAM, that compressed smaller will be able to fit. However, serious users should buy a gaming GPU with 24GB of VRAM or more, either by stacking up GPUs or by buying specific AI racks or machines with unified memory like the Mac Mini or the Nvidia DGX Spark.
Quantization shrinks a model by storing each weight with fewer bits. Hugging Face's documentation describes it as representing weights and activations "with low-precision data types like 8-bit integer (int8) instead of the usual 32-bit floating point (float32)," which cuts memory use at the cost of some accuracy.
LM Studio's system requirements recommend 16GB or more of RAM on Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or newer, though 8GB Macs can handle smaller models. On Windows it recommends at least 16GB of RAM and 4GB of dedicated VRAM, with AVX2 processor support, and Intel-based Macs are not supported.
Ollama's library lists Gemma 4 26B at 16 to 19GB and the 31B version at 19 to 20GB. OpenAI's gpt-oss-20b needs only 16GB of memory, and gpt-oss-120b runs within 80GB, according to OpenAI.
How to set up Ollama and LM Studio
LM Studio is probably the go-to choice because it provides a nice polished graphical user interface. Ollama, on the other hand, is aimed at developers and more experienced users who prefer working inside of a terminal (CLI).
For LM Studio, download the installer for your operating system from lmstudio.ai, search for a model inside the app, download its weights and open a chat. The app searches Hugging Face, the public hub where open models are published.
For Ollama, macOS and Linux users install with the command curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh, and Windows users run irm https://ollama.com/install.ps1 | iex in PowerShell, both listed on Ollama's download page.
Typing ollama pull gemma4:e2b downloads a model and ollama run gemma4:e2b opens a chat, and /bye exits, per Ollama's quickstart. The program also opens a local API at http://localhost:11434, so other apps on your machine can use the model.
Model names ending in ":cloud," such as gemma4:cloud, are cloud models that run in Ollama's cloud and need no download, so skip those if privacy is the point. That said, this is a good second option for those who need more powerful models: The calls and prompts handled over API are not stored in the providers’ servers, and are not used to train models.
Google's Multi-Token Prediction drafters for Gemma 4, available on Ollama under Apache 2.0, speed up generation by up to 3x using speculative decoding, in which a small model proposes several tokens ahead and the large one checks them together.
Google said that "if the target model agrees with the draft, it accepts the entire sequence in a single forward pass," and the target model adds one extra token of its own in that same pass.
Local models gain web search and file access through MCP servers, short for Model Context Protocol, and LM Studio added support in version 0.3.17, according to the Decrypt guide.
Where local models still lose to the cloud
The four-month average describes the most capable open models, and the largest are far past consumer hardware. Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max has 2.4 trillion total parameters, with 95 billion active at any time, compared with the 80GB of memory that gpt-oss-120b runs within.
When a model spills out of VRAM into system RAM, responses may be a lot slower, and larger context windows need more memory. Gemma 4's small models offer a 128K-token context window, the amount of text a model can consider at once, and the larger ones 256K.
Cloud services need none of that planning, and the frontier models behind them still lead on the hardest tests.
If you want to use AI privately, our own review recommended "xPrivo with a self-hosted local model for day-to-day drafting that must not leave your machine," and Kagi "when you need web retrieval and accept the API call tradeoff."

items.content:
Issuer Objections to OKXICE Tokenized Stocks Expand to 50 Companies

The number of companies objecting to the tokenization of their shares on OKXICE TSV, a joint venture between OKX and NYSE parent ICE, has risen to 50, with Nvidia, Micron, Nike, Costco and Reddit among the latest additions. OKXICE had initially planned to offer tokenized trading in shares of 62 companies. Under the SEC’s temporary conditional exemption, issuers may submit a written objection within 30 calendar days of receiving notice to prevent tokenized versions of their shares, issued by an unaffiliated third party, from being traded on the venue. — link

items.author: Cointelegraph by Michael Millard
items.content:
DeepSeek developing AI agent requiring less human input: Report
The proposal comes amid intense competition among AI developers, including US companies Anthropic and OpenAI, the SCMP said.
Chinese artificial intelligence company DeepSeek has revealed a design to increase the autonomy of AI coding assistants so they can perform multiple tasks with less human intervention.
The aim is to reduce human input in coordinating and monitoring multiple AI agents, according to a paper published by the company’s DeepSeek Harness team and reported by Singapore’s South China Morning Post on Sunday.
Managing multiple agents demands human attention, the team said, noting that “single-task limits depend on model capabilities, while multitask limits depend on human attention.”
The DeepSeek paper said a person can oversee only three to five active AI agent sessions simultaneously. Its proposed system would distribute tasks among agents and coordinate their work, leaving humans free to review results and make decisions.
The proposal comes amid intense competition among AI developers, including US companies Anthropic and OpenAI, according to the SCMP.
Cointelegraph reported last October that Chinese artificial intelligence models were outperforming US counterparts in cryptocurrency trading, according to data from blockchain analytics platform CoinGlass.
AI chatbot DeepSeek led a crypto trading experiment, being the only AI model to generate a positive unrealized return of 9.1%. The results surprised crypto traders, given that DeepSeek was developed at a fraction of the cost of its US rivals.

所谓「帝国 CEO」，并不只是公司老板权力大，而是这些科技巨头越来越像围绕创始人意志运转的王国。他们可以押上数百亿美元，追逐近乎科幻的技术愿景。即便上市融资，也不必像传统企业高管那样受到股东的直接约束。

扎克伯格曾豪赌元宇宙，投入数百亿美元，如今又大举押注 AI。Meta 董事会最近甚至为他设计了新的无投票权股票，以应对潜在的加州富豪税，同时保住他的控制权。

马斯克手中的 SpaceX 已将火箭、星链、X 和 Grok 纳入同一商业版图，上市后依然由他主导。

Anthropic 则准备让七名创始人与独立信托共同把持公司治理，试图让 AI 安全路线不受短期股价压力左右。

硅谷推崇这种敢于豪赌的「创始人模式」，投资者也愿意为之买单。但赌对了，投资者可能获得惊人回报；赌错了，外部股东却很难纠正方向。

当科技巨头的决策影响越来越多人的生活，谁来约束这些「帝国 CEO」，便不再只是股东自己的问题。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Michael Millard
items.content:
Binance says phase one of withdrawals opens after $6.3B hack
The crypto exchange said it has begun phased withdrawals after the record hack the FBI has blamed on North Korea.
Binance said it has reopened its Bitcoin network in phase one of resuming withdrawals after a major hack of about $6.3 billion in funds.
The crypto exchange had suspended user withdrawals after the attack on Thursday, which the FBI blamed on North Korean operatives.
“First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals is $BTC bitcoin network,” Binance said on X.
In an earlier X announcement on Sunday, Binance had said it would roll out withdrawal services in phases, which will be progressively available. Updates will be available on its official X channel, it added.
“We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” Binance said.
Users should check the withdrawal page for their selected asset and network, or visit the Binance network status page to confirm availability, the company said.
During the phased rollout, it is expected that there will be some congestion, longer processing times and even temporary delays, Binance said, so if a withdrawal is not successful, users should try again after a short while.
Cointelegraph reported on Saturday that Binance said it had replenished 90% of the assets stolen in the hack, up from 80% a day earlier, and remained on track to resume withdrawals Sunday.
Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

高盛内部对AI行情出现分歧：一方警告盈利增长见顶，另一方称1.1万亿美元订单已验证投资回报

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 1 日，高盛两位资深策略师对 AI 行情前景给出截然不同的判断。Tony Pasquariello 认为，科技巨头第三季度财报暴露出标普 500 盈利增长可能已经见顶，市场上行动能正在减弱，目前不宜大举押注；伦敦策略师 Mark Wilson 则认为，谷歌云和 AWS 合计约 1.1 万亿美元的积压订单，已经相当明确地证明 AI 投资回报正在兑现，维持看多立场。

Wilson 援引的数据包括：谷歌云营收同比增长 103%，积压订单增长 256% 至 5610 亿美元；AWS 营收增长 39%，积压订单增长 189% 至 5780 亿美元，两者积压订单合计约 1.14 万亿美元。Wilson 认为，全球大型云服务商的增长表现说明 AI 需求依然强劲，市场对投资回报的质疑正在得到回应。

但 Pasquariello 认为，亮眼的云业务增长掩盖了其他核心业务的疲软，科技巨头持续扩大资本开支，却未能同步证明盈利增长空间。他指出，标普 500 盈利增长已显现见顶迹象，远期每股收益预期上调幅度也明显放缓。

市场当前的核心争议，已从 AI 需求是否存在转向投资回报如何兑现。Alphabet 尽管拥有 5610 亿美元云业务积压订单，本季度仍录得 9.1 亿美元自由现金流净流出，低于市场预期的 35 亿美元净流入。高盛另一位策略师 Rich Privorotsky 则将问题归结为「价值捕获」：AI 产业链中究竟哪些企业能够真正盈利，以及需要付出多高的融资成本。

与此同时，美股内部走势出现明显分化，剔除 AI 股的标普 500 指数 10 月表现显著强于科技股。两位策略师均认为市场波动异常，但对 AI 行情能否延续仍持不同判断。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Michael Millard
items.content:
FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack
US agency seeks private-sector help to block further money-laundering of stolen digital assets.
The FBI said that the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of about $6.3 billion in digital assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance on Thursday.
The FBI said on Saturday in a news release that it refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as “TraderTraitor,” which it has most recently observed converting stolen assets mostly into Ether (ETH).
It expects these assets to be further converted, using DeFi and instant swap services, as the hackers move to more advanced laundering stages.
The FBI urged private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets. A full list of addresses is provided on the news release.
Cointelegraph reported earlier this year that North Korea-linked hackers stole about 60% of the value lost to crypto hacks in 2025, with proceeds used to help fund the regime’s nuclear and ballistic missile programs, highlighting a growing reliance on digital assets to generate hard currency.
North Korean defense spending supplemented
Related: Crypto losses from North Korea hackers in 2025 rose 51% YoY: Report
Those findings came from a CertiK report that attributed more than $2 billion of an estimated $3.4 billion in 2025 crypto security losses to groups tied North Korea, across 79 of 656 incidents documented that year.
While North Korea does not publish credible budget data, according to independent research organization MilitarySpend, mid-range consensus places its actual annual defense spending at as much as $6 billion, using purchasing-power-adjusted GDP estimates, though this figure is uncertain.
MilitarySpend adds that revenue from Russia arms transfers — estimated at as much as $5 billion in munitions exported to Russia from 2022-2025 per South Korean intelligence — supplements domestic weapons programs, as does cryptocurrency theft, which provides additional off-budget financing for WMD development.
As Cointelegraph reported, between 2016 and early 2026, North Korea-linked actors stole an estimated $6.75 billion in cryptocurrency across 263 documented incidents, according to CertiK, citing findings by independent onchain researcher Taylor Monahan.
CertiK’s analysis concluded that North Korea has industrialized crypto theft into a core state revenue mechanism.
Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen
items.title: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack

items.author: wublockchainenglish
items.content:
OneKey Founder: Some Older iPhones Have Unpatchable Chip Vulnerabilities, Posing Risks to Seed Phrase Storage

OneKey founder Yishi warned that factory-resetting an older iPhone, enabling airplane mode, and using it to store crypto wallet seed phrases offline may still be unsafe. He noted that iPhone 4S through iPhone X are affected by checkm8, while iPhone XS, XR, 11 series, and second-generation iPhone SE are affected by usbliter8, disclosed earlier this year. These BootROM-level vulnerabilities cannot be fixed through iOS updates. Attackers with physical access and specialized tools may exploit them via USB, even in airplane mode.

However, on models such as the XS and 11, these flaws alone do not provide direct access to seed phrases, as device passcodes and the Secure Enclave offer additional protection. Yishi advised affected users to generate entirely new seed phrases in a trusted environment, transfer their assets, use newer devices, keep software updated, and adopt stronger passwords. — link

xAI没签欧盟透明准则，Grok API却要在全球默认加文字水印

动察 Beating AI 快讯，xAI 更新开发文档，宣布从 11 月 7 日起，为 Grok 4.7、4.6、4.5、4.3 及三款 Grok 4.20 模型的 API 输出默认加入隐形文字水印。不只欧盟，全球及区域 API 都在覆盖范围内，连结构化输出和工具调用参数也会被标记。目前尚未明确 Grok 网页版和 X 内置聊天是否同步启用。

这种水印通过在模型生成文本时，轻微调整选词概率，让整段文字留下可识别的统计规律。直接复制粘贴不会消除水印，但缩短文本、大幅改写会降低检测可靠性。

背后是欧盟《AI 法案》的透明度要求，相关规定已于 8 月 2 日开始适用。虽然 xAI 没有签署欧盟的自愿性透明准则，但仍须遵守适用的法律义务。开发者团队可以按模型关闭水印，不过必须确认符合相关法律豁免，并自行承担标记和披露责任。

Google 早在 2024 年就将 SynthID 文字水印用于 Gemini，Anthropic 今年 8 月开始为 Claude 新模型在全球启用水印。OpenAI 则在 10 月宣布，逐步为欧盟地区的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 加水印，同时允许全球 API 用户主动开启，默认仍关闭。

Meta联手傅利叶3个月造出人形机器人原型，想给Muse装上手和脚

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Meta 与上海傅利叶智能合作，仅用三个月造出人形机器人原型 Max。Max 基于傅利叶前三代人形机器人的硬件和技术积累开发，Meta 主要调整了机身比例、头部设计和摄像头，并增加了双手等部件。Meta 机器人产品副总裁还在傅利叶上海工厂待了近两个月，8 月底完成内部展示。

Meta 去年成立机器人团队时，就想做机器人界的「安卓」：自己研发 AI 软件，让不同厂商的机器人都能使用。CTO Bosworth 当时指出，机器人跑跳已经不算最难，真正的瓶颈是精细操作。比如拿起一杯水，既不能捏碎杯子，也不能把水洒出来。这需要 AI 理解物理世界，并掌握对力度和动作的精确控制。

与傅利叶合作，让 Meta 不必从零开发机器人本体，就能更快开展这类实验。Max 高约 1.5 米，搭载英伟达 Jetson Thor 芯片，五指手可以拿起小瓶子和玩具。双方 9 月又启动 Max 2，重点改进双手操作和上下楼梯能力。

Meta 希望未来让 Muse AI 智能体拥有身体，进入家庭完成实际任务。

OpenAI、Google等四巨头统一AI训练拒绝规则，网站不用再逐家设置

动察 Beating AI 快讯，OpenAI、Google、微软和 Anthropic 达成一致：以后网站只需在 `robots.txt` 中添加 `User-Agent: __usage_ai-training` 和 `Disallow: /` 两条规则，就能同时告诉这几家公司，不要拿自己的内容训练 AI。过去，网站需要分别针对 GPTBot、ClaudeBot 等爬虫设置规则。

这套规则只针对 AI 训练，不会一并禁止爬虫抓取网站，也不一定影响 AI 在回答中引用网站内容。它由 Anthropic 工程师提出，目前还是互联网工程任务组（IETF）的技术草案。

各家公司对规则的执行方式不完全一样。微软允许网站单独禁止 AI 训练，同时保留内容被 AI 搜索引用的机会。Google 则计划把这条规则与现有的 Google-Extended 设置绑定，可能连 Gemini 引用网站内容也一起限制。

Anthropic 已开始采用，微软计划在 2027 年 2 月生效，Google 计划 2027 年支持，OpenAI 也将在未来数月上线。

但这些规则不能撤回此前已经用于训练的数据，也无法强制 AI 公司遵守。

AI融资、财报与政治风险三重夹击，市场开始拷问行业投资回报

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 1 日，AI 热潮正遭遇债券市场、企业财报和美国政治风险的三重压力。随着融资门槛抬高、科技巨头自由现金流恶化，以及数据中心建设引发的公众反对声浪扩大，投资者正从追逐算力增长转向审视 AI 投资能否兑现回报。

债券市场率先释放压力。CoreWeave、Nebius 和 Nscale 等 AI 云服务商近期几乎被挡在高收益债券发行市场之外。CoreWeave 今年早些时候发行的 9.75% 票息债券，目前二级市场收益率已超过 15%。美国企业债市场 AI 相关发行规模从 2025 年的 3940 亿美元升至今年截至 10 月中旬的 6550 亿美元，分析师预计明年新增 AI 相关债务规模可能接近 1 万亿美元。融资供应激增与投资者风险敞口集中，正在推高企业融资成本。

财报季进一步加剧市场担忧。Alphabet 连续第二个季度出现负自由现金流，财报后股价单日暴跌 13%，市值蒸发约 5000 亿美元；Amazon 当季负自由现金流接近 350 亿美元，Meta 则因提高资本开支计划而承压，标普已将其信用评级展望下调至负面。四家大型云厂商中，只有微软当季录得正自由现金流，达到 186 亿美元。

AI 带来的冲击也蔓延至软件行业。ServiceNow 因季度销售展望不及预期，股价单日暴跌 31%；Twilio 下跌 18%。市场开始担心生成式 AI 产品可能削弱传统软件公司的定价能力和利润率。

政治风险则成为另一项不确定因素。美国中期选举临近，数据中心建设引发的电价、环境和就业争议持续升温。民调显示，约三分之二美国人反对新建数据中心。若民主党重新掌控国会，AI 行业可能面临更密集的调查、听证和监管审查，数据中心建设及运营成本也可能受到影响。

市场的核心变化在于，AI 投资正从规模竞赛进入回报验证阶段。债权人要求更高收益率和更严格保护条款，股票投资者则更加关注自由现金流、资本开支纪律及盈利能力。AI 需求仍然强劲，但仅凭扩大算力投入已不足以支撑估值，能否将巨额资本开支转化为实际收入和利润，正成为企业之间的关键分水岭。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/374853

Troves遭攻击损失约8.6枚BTC，已向攻击者提供1枚WBTC白帽赏金

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 1 日，BTCFi 协议 Troves 发文表示，今晨其 xWBTC/WBTC 金库遭遇攻击，初步估计损失约 8.6 枚 BTC。目前调查显示，攻击范围仅限于该金库，其他 Troves 金库暂未发现受到影响。

Troves 表示，此次攻击涉及一份已被替换但仍保留权限的旧版再平衡合约。团队已撤销相关合约权限，并出于安全考虑暂停受影响及可能存在风险的金库。目前正与安全合作伙伴追踪被盗资金，并评估追回方案。

此外，Troves 已通过链上消息向攻击者提出白帽赏金方案，承诺在归还剩余资金后支付 1 枚 WBTC 作为奖励。团队表示，后续将公布详细事件复盘及受影响存款用户的处理方案。

items.content:
YC支持的「无声打字」眼镜：号称每分钟200词，原型还拖着电路板

动察 Beating AI 快讯，YC 孵化的初创公司 Subvocal 宣布累计获得 130 万美元融资，正在开发一副「无声打字」眼镜。用户只要轻轻做出说话口型，不必发声或碰键盘，文字就能输入电脑。写邮件、记笔记，甚至给 AI Agent 下指令都可以这样完成。团队宣称，原型每分钟能连续转写超过 200 个词。

眼镜通过低功率射频信号，捕捉面部发音肌肉的细微运动，再由 AI 模型解码。用户依然得动嘴，只是不需要发出声音。

类似技术并非首次出现。MIT 早在 2018 年就推出过 AlterEgo，靠贴在面部的电极识别无声语音，但当时主要在约 20 词的限定词表中测试。Subvocal 想进一步实现无接触、不限词汇的持续输入。

不过，产品距离真正上市还有一段距离。目前的演示原型仍拖着外置电路板，和计划推出的眼镜形态差别不小。每分钟超过 200 词的速度，也没有经过公开的独立评测验证。

Subvocal 已在美国开放预订，早鸟总价 499 美元，先付可退款的 199 美元订金。公司预计 2027 年第一季度开始发货，仍需获得 FCC 批准。

Baseten拟融资20亿美元，最高估值300亿：4个月身价翻倍有余

动察 Beating AI 快讯，AI 推理平台 Baseten 正筹划约 20 亿美元新融资。彭博社披露，本轮拟分两档定价：第一档估值 260 亿美元，第二档 300 亿美元。现有投资者 Sands Capital 预计领投，交易尚未完成。

Baseten 今年 1 月估值只有 50 亿美元，6 月刚以 130 亿美元估值完成 15 亿美元融资。如果新一轮按最高档成交，9 个月内估值将升至原来的 6 倍。值得注意的是，6 月那轮融资也曾被报道采用双档定价，分别为 110 亿和 130 亿美元。

Baseten 主要帮企业部署和运行 AI 模型，处理 GPU 算力调度、推理优化等工作。Cursor、Notion、OpenEvidence 等都是其客户。公司今年 6 月披露，过去一年收入增长 20 倍，推理用量增长 40 倍。

随着企业大量部署开源和定制模型，推理平台迎来快速增长。

下周宏观展望：美国中期选举与非农数据成市场焦点，美股迎苹果、AMD财报

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 1 日，11 月 2 日至 8 日当周，全球市场将迎来多项重磅事件。美国中期选举、苹果与 AMD 财报以及 10 月非农就业数据将成为市场关注焦点，此外，英国央行、澳大利亚央行利率决议、以色列议会选举结果及俄美乌三方谈判进展也值得关注。

科技股方面，苹果和 AMD 将公布最新财报，成为 AI 交易信心遭遇冲击后的重要检验。苹果市场预期营收约 1130 亿美元，这也是新任 CEO 特努斯上任后的首次财报；AMD 市场预期营收约 130 亿美元，Helios 机柜及 MI450 芯片的推进情况将受到关注。此外，高通、超微电脑、Coherent、Lumentum 及伯克希尔哈撒韦也将公布业绩。另有报道称，Marvell 正就收购 Lumentum 进行磋商，最快可能于下周宣布。苹果 Apple 智能接入阿里千问的测试则计划于 11 月 4 日开放。

政治与地缘方面，11 月 3 日美国中期选举将改选众议院全部 435 个席位及参议院 35 个席位，选举结果将影响特朗普政府未来两年的财政、关税及产业政策推进空间。11 月 4 日以色列议会选举最终结果预计公布，俄美乌三方谈判也计划于下周在阿布扎比重启。

宏观数据方面，美国 10 月非农就业报告将公布。此前 9 月非农新增就业仅 2.9 万人，市场预期 10 月新增 6.5 万人。若就业数据表现强劲，可能进一步强化市场对美联储 12 月加息的预期，并影响美元、美债及黄金走势。中国 10 月外汇储备数据也将出炉。

OpenCode重新支持Claude订阅：3月被迫移除，这次拿到了许可

动察 Beating AI 快讯，开源 AI 编程工具 OpenCode 在 v2.2.3 中重新支持 Claude 订阅。用户只需安装并登录 Claude Code，再到 OpenCode 中选择「Claude Agent」，就能直接使用原有订阅额度，无需额外购买 API。

今年 3 月，OpenCode 曾因 Anthropic 的法务要求，移除内置的 Claude 订阅登录插件。这次改走官方 Claude Agent SDK，调用用户本机安装的 Claude Code，由后者直接向 Anthropic 发送模型请求。OpenCode 不读取登录凭证。

开发者 Daniel Smolsky 还在 GitHub 上明确表示，团队已获得 Anthropic 许可，符合服务条款。

OpenAI官宣12月合并ChatGPT和Codex额度：普通聊天也要抢编程额度，但Instant除外

动察 Beating AI 快讯，此前被「光头哥」Tibor Blaho 从 ChatGPT 订阅页面扒出的共享额度规则，现在得到了官方确认。

OpenAI 最新帮助文档明确，12 月起 Plus、Pro 和 Business 用户的 ChatGPT 与 Codex 将共用一份额度，同时把 ChatGPT Work 的 Agent 能力整合进普通聊天界面。

届时，使用量将统一按 Token 计算，模型越强、任务越复杂，消耗的额度通常越多。不过 Instant 模式聊天不扣共享额度。用户可以在设置中查看剩余额度和重置时间。

讽刺的是，OpenAI 前脚才宣布 Pro 等套餐额度翻倍，后脚就确认要把聊天和编程放进同一个额度池。

官方还安慰用户，预计大多数用户不会比现在更频繁地耗尽额度。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/374846

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 1 日，在人工智能热潮持续推动下，韩国出口 10 月继续保持强劲增长，外贸依赖型经济的出口势头进一步增强。

韩国贸易、工业和资源部周日公布的数据显示，经工作日差异调整后，韩国 10 月出口额同比增长 76.1%，达到 1153 亿美元，低于前一个月创下的 1211 亿美元纪录。未经调整的数据显示，10 月出口额同比增长 93.7%，进口额增长 36%，实现贸易顺差 425 亿美元，韩国 9 月出口额同比增幅经修正后为 83.7%。

出口持续强劲，进一步强化了市场对韩国央行本月加息的预期。半导体仍是出口增长的主要驱动力。10 月韩国芯片出口额同比激增 259%，达到 564 亿美元；计算机出口增长 497%，石油产品和汽车出口分别增长 80% 和 18%。(金十)

Binance Co-CEO: Attackers Used Self-Destruct Mechanisms, Making the Hack Harder to Trace

Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng updated the investigation into the roughly $6.3 billion hack on October 30, saying multiple people were involved. Investigators initially suspected a compromised laptop but later found other entry points. Attackers used self-destruct mechanisms to erase tools and traces, complicating the investigation. Teng said they used EIP-7702 to gain on-chain execution authority over a hot wallet without passing Binance's normal approval controls. Binance paused withdrawals to rebuild and test its systems, targeting restoration within 40 hours. It is also working with law enforcement to trace and recover stolen funds. — link

items.content:
North Korean Hackers Moved $38M Through Relay Protocol in 7 Hours

On-chain analyst Specter reported that North Korean hackers transferred approximately $38 million through Relay Protocol within seven hours, with transfers still ongoing at the time of the post. Despite Relay's claims of having a Know Your Transaction (KYT) monitoring system in place, it failed to block the transfers.

Specter noted that North Korean hackers would have struggled to move such a large amount through THORChain in the same timeframe, raising questions about Relay's compliance and risk controls. Relay Protocol is a cross-chain bridge and interoperability protocol that enables asset transfers across multiple blockchains. — link

谷歌正探索在AI购物流程中引入商品比较、优惠和赞助链接

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Alphabet 近期财报显示，谷歌搜索查询量同比增速达到五年来最高，但 AI Mode 变现水平仍然偏低，拖累搜索业务收入表现。谷歌第三季度搜索收入同比增长 12%，但低于市场预期；包含搜索等业务的谷歌服务部门收入为 963 亿美元，也未达到分析师预期的 985 亿美元。

谷歌首席商务官菲利普·辛德勒表示，AI Mode 查询量增长强劲，但目前变现水平较低。AI Mode 中的查询平均长度约为传统搜索的 3 倍，约五分之一的查询通过语音、图片或文档完成。CEO 皮查伊称，公司将优先改善搜索体验，再逐步推进商业化。

为寻找新的收入增长点，谷歌正探索在 AI 购物流程中引入商品比较、优惠和赞助链接，让 AI 代理负责搜集信息、筛选商品，同时保留用户比较品牌、价格和服务的环节。谷歌此前已测试在旅行规划中展示优惠，以及在 AI 生成的商品列表中加入明确标识的赞助链接，并计划将 AI Mode 和 AI Overviews 中的广告扩展至更多查询。

皮查伊还表示，谷歌将把代理功能进一步引入搜索和 Gemini，并扩展至 Chrome、Android 和 Workspace 等产品。

OneKey创始人：旧款iPhone存储助记词存在硬件级风险，飞行模式也无法防护

BlockBeats 消息，11 月 1 日，OneKey 创始人 Yishi 发文提醒，将旧款 iPhone 恢复出厂设置、开启飞行模式并专门用于存储钱包助记词，并不意味着安全。iPhone 11 及更早机型存在无法通过 iOS 更新修复的 BootROM 硬件漏洞，攻击者在取得设备实体访问权限后，可通过 USB 接口和自定义硬件在 iOS 启动前执行代码，飞行模式无法阻止此类攻击。

Yishi 提到，iPhone 4S 至 iPhone X 存在 2019 年公开的 checkm8 漏洞，iPhone XS、XR、11 系列及第二代 iPhone SE 则受到今年 6 月公开的 usbliter8 研究影响。不过，BootROM 漏洞本身并不意味着攻击者可以直接获取助记词，设备密码、Secure Enclave 等防护仍然存在，但旧版系统、简单密码及钱包应用较弱的加密机制可能进一步扩大风险。

此外，旧版 iOS 还可能受到恶意充电设备攻击。Yishi 建议，使用 iPhone 存储助记词的用户应迁移至 iPhone 12 或更新机型，并在可信环境中生成全新的助记词、转移资产；同时使用较长的字母数字密码，避免使用公共 USB 充电接口。若设备曾长时间脱离本人控制，也应尽快迁移资产。

其还提醒，iPhone 12 及更新机型目前没有公开的同类 BootROM 漏洞；旧款设备的风险则存在于芯片层面，无法单靠更新系统消除。

FBI Attributes Over $6B Binance Hack to North Korea, Urges THORNode Operators and Other Crypto Service Providers to Block Money Laundering-Linked Transactions

The FBI attributed the theft of more than $6 billion in crypto assets from Binance to North Korean hackers, identifying the malicious cyber activity as TraderTraitor. The FBI, US Secret Service (USSS), and IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI) observed the attackers converting stolen assets primarily into ETH, with further laundering expected through DeFi and instant swap services. The agencies urged THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms, and other virtual asset service providers to block transactions involving or derived from addresses used by the attackers to launder the stolen funds. The FBI also published a list of addresses operated by or closely linked to the attackers that currently hold or previously held stolen assets. — link

items.content:
YouTube-style UI over 6,454 videos sourced from 39,834 HN comments since 2007.

https://hackertube.org/ --- Top Comments --- [murm]: It's so refreshing browsing this compared to YouTube, it feels like I don't have to constantly be on high alert at being baited into some trap. Makes you wonder what kind of internet could be possible if all these tech giants weren't just optimizing for engagement and addiction. [zmmmmm]: I've been a bit fascinated by my lack of interest in the feeds that are curated for me. They are all things I'm supposedly interested in but I just am not when I see them in that format. I realised after a while that one of the main reasons I go online is to expand my horizons. I'm actively looking for something new or interesting or surprising that I might not have encountered or thought about before. I am also looking for perspective - give me a broad picture of how the wor... [minimaxa]: You know what I like about this? It's 100% pure nerd content, no sneaky influencer videos or clickbaity news. It does need a new-to-old sort though, which is easy to add in. If you watched all of these videos, you would be the smartest, most annoying person ever. Lol [genxy]: Wonderful! > Fork it > Everything behind this site is yours to reuse. The easiest way: give the zip to your AI agent (Claude Code or similar) and tell it what you want, such as a different interface, a weekly email of talks on your topics, a terminal browser, or an analysis. The zip includes a DATA.md written for agents: how the files fit together, the gotchas, example records, and how to walk you through getting YouTube metadata if you want it. https://hackertube.org/about [reorder9695]: I find it amazing how close the front page of this is to what I actually watch/want to watch on YouTube. I guess I shouldn't be surprised, but it feels like an unpersonalised feed (besides being based on Hacker News) shouldn't have a significantly better hitrate for me than YouTube's "personalised" feed.

--- Top Comments ---

[asveikau]: > TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 / CVSS 9.8 I know it's customary for HN to edit titles to remove extraneous information, but removing "Linux" here really takes away something useful and relevant.  This is a Linux vulnerability.  If you're running *BSD or Mac or Windows, not affected.

[peanut-walrus]: Some notes I've got about this: - MPTCP is not a requirement, it is a generic use-after-free. - Exploitability over the internet is unlikely, most ISP routers drop packets with IP options fields. - At least according to Red Hat, dropping packets with IP options yourself helps, but is not a full mitigation. - Successful exploit requires multiple CPU cores to process packets, so systems with just a single core or packet processing pinned to a single core are not affected.

[swinglock]: How are Ubuntu and RHEL not fixed? Few operating systems market themselves more as suitable for servers. What are they doing over there?

[grey-area]: No patches for Ubuntu or red hat yet.  https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-98432   https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2026-98432

[dhx]: Fixed upstream in:[1] 7.3 (2026-10-18) 7.2.10 (2026-10-11) 6.18.56 (2026-10-11) 6.12.113 (2026-10-15) 6.6.159 (2026-10-15) 6.1.190 (2026-10-15) 5.15.225 (2026-10-15) [1]  https://lore.kernel.org/all/?q=tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor  -- check for "kfree_rcu" being used instead of "kfree" within "tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor" (net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c)

Chainalysis: Ethereum Reorg Triggers THORChain Emergency Pause, Delaying Laundering of Binance Hack Funds

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said an Ethereum chain reorganization on the morning of October 31 (EDT) caused THORChain to mistakenly issue a double refund to a user who had deposited 10 ETH, triggering an emergency pause. The pause blocked cross-chain swaps through most of THORChain’s bridges for all users, including North Korean money launderers, inadvertently delaying the laundering of a significant amount of funds stolen from Binance. — link

items.content:
开源版「豆包手机助手」来了：能在后台操作微信，不耽误你刷手机

动察 Beating AI 快讯，独立开发者王赞开源了一款名叫 Mika 的安卓 AI 助手，能直接操控手机上的微信、小红书等 App，帮用户整理聊天记录、发送消息。

作者演示了让 Mika 在后台翻阅微信群聊、总结聊天记录，还能给微信文件传输助手发消息。整个过程中，用户可以继续在主屏幕使用其他 App，不必把屏幕让给 AI。

豆包手机助手依靠手机厂商提供系统级权限，Mika 则通过安卓无线调试启动一个具有 Shell 权限的辅助进程，在普通手机上创建一块看不见的虚拟屏幕，让微信等 App 在上面运行。AI 通过无障碍服务读取按钮、文字和输入框，执行点击、滑动和输入；遇到控件无法识别的界面，就用本地 OCR 或视觉模型看图操作。

Mika 首次使用需要开启开发者选项、完成无线调试配对并授权无障碍服务。模型可以自行配置 API，也支持通过 ChatGPT 账号登录。运行时无需连接电脑，电脑上的 Codex 等工具还可以通过 MCP 向它派发任务。

Android 12 起即可使用跨 App 操作功能。到了 Android 14，Mika 可以利用虚拟屏幕的独立焦点能力，在后台操作时不抢占主屏幕的输入焦点。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Bryan O'Shea
items.content:
Binance says 90% of stolen assets replenished, targets Sunday withdrawals
Less-liquid tokens make up the remaining shortfall as Binance continues buying replacement assets through market and over-the-counter trades.
Binance said Saturday it had replenished 90% of the assets stolen in its $6.3 billion hack, up from 80% a day earlier, and remained on track to resume withdrawals Sunday.
The exchange is using a combination of its corporate treasury, a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and a portion of its futures insurance fund, a spokesperson told Cointelegraph.
“Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not users,” the spokesperson said, adding that the insurance fund would remain above required risk management levels.
The update follows Thursday’s theft, the largest cryptocurrency hack on record, which TRM Labs has since attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacker group.
Following the hack, Binance said Friday it had set aside $6.34 billion to cover losses, including $5 billion in the affected cryptocurrencies. Industry partners like Tether and Circle froze about $3 billion in affected assets after the hack, but those funds are separate from Binance’s replacement of stolen tokens.
Still, CertiK told Cointelegraph on Friday that it needed more information to verify Binance’s claimed $5 billion in replacement cryptocurrencies. Binance has since published a new reserves snapshot, but says the full cryptographic proof is still being generated. “The full zero-knowledge proof takes approximately 40 to 50 hours to generate due to the computational workload,” the exchange’s update reads.
Binance said in its update on X that customer balances in Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and eight other assets were fully backed. The remaining shortfall consists of less liquid tokens that it continues to buy through market and over-the-counter transactions, the update reads.
The spokesperson’s statement did not specify how much each funding source contributed or disclose the insurance fund’s minimum required balance. It also did not quantify how much stolen crypto had been recovered.
Read Cointelegraph’s full coverage of the Binance hack here.

AI投入回报担忧加剧，纳指100指数10月跌6.7%，创2025年3月以来最差月度表现

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，据彭博社报道，科技巨头最新财报未能缓解投资者对 AI 基础设施投入回报的担忧。尽管云计算业务继续增长，数据中心建设对自由现金流的消耗仍引发抛售，纳斯达克 100 指数 10 月累计下跌 6.7%，创 2025 年 3 月以来最差月度表现。四家超大规模云厂商中，亚马逊、Meta 和 Alphabet 本季均录得自由现金流缺口，其中亚马逊缺口接近 350 亿美元。微软是例外，自由现金流为正 186 亿美元，Azure 收入增速也超过预期，但股价周五仍下跌 1.6%。

Alphabet 周四下跌 13%，创历史最差单日表现。公司连续第二个季度自由现金流为负，核心搜索业务收入也令人失望。搜索业务去年贡献了公司近 56% 的收入，使 AI 扩张可能蚕食核心业务的风险受到关注。Meta 自 10 月 21 日公布财报、提高年度资本开支计划以来，股价累计下跌 12%。标普全球评级周五将其信用评级展望由稳定调整为负面，指出尚不明确这些支出何时能够产生超过成本增长的收入。与此同时，资本投入仍在推进：Meta 未来支出承诺升至 8250 亿美元，Alphabet 未来支出义务则超过 1 万亿美元。

担忧也蔓延至软件行业。ServiceNow 季度销售指引不及预期，股价周四创纪录下跌 31%；Twilio 因指引令人失望，周五下跌 18%；Fortinet 下调服务销售预测，引发网络安全股抛售。投资者担忧 Anthropic、OpenAI 等公司的产品可能侵蚀软件企业的定价能力与利润率。

Fifth Third Wealth Advisors 首席投资官 Chris Osmond 认为，投资者开始奖励能够将支出转化为收入和实际回报的企业，并惩罚尚未实现转化、或继续增加支出的企业。Ameriprise 首席市场策略师 Anthony Saglimbene 则指出，科技巨头正从轻资产、高现金流企业变成重资产企业，现金流及增长可靠性发生变化，因此需要不同的估值方式。他认为，AI 接下来将进入「证明自己」的阶段，每季财报都会检验市场此前的高预期。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Nate Kostar
items.content:
Bitcoin held up better than expected after Binance hack, Strive CEO says
Strive CEO Matt Cole says the Binance hack has not changed his long-term case for Bitcoin, but cautions it is too early to call a market bottom.
Bitcoin has held up better than expected following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to Strive CEO Matt Cole, who said the breach does not undermine the cryptocurrency’s long-term investment thesis.
Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction on Friday, Cole said the breach had not changed his long-term investment case for Bitcoin. He compared the attack on Binance’s wallets to a bank robbery rather than a failure of Bitcoin’s network.
Bitcoin traded near $77,400 at 4:00 pm on Saturday, about 4% below its price shortly before the attack began Thursday, according to CoinGecko data.
Strive, a publicly traded company that holds Bitcoin on its balance sheet, reported owning 43,000 BTC as of Oct. 23.
“I do have conviction that over any reasonable time frame, this does not change the investment thesis on Bitcoin,” Cole said.
Cole said Bitcoin’s decline was less severe than he expected given the scale of the breach and broader market weakness, although he acknowledged that it was too early to determine whether the cryptocurrency had reached a price bottom.
Cole described the market as being in an “early spring” recovery phase that could last another six to nine months, with prices gradually rising rather than surging to new highs.
Paul Chapman, financial crime director at Wirex, also distinguished the attack on Binance from a compromise of Bitcoin’s network. “It’s important to be clear that Bitcoin itself hasn’t been hacked — this was an attack on one company’s systems, not the network,” he told Cointelegraph.
Related: Strive closes $630M SATS IPO, leaves Bitcoin allocation unspecified
Bitcoin reaction compared with Bybit
According to Glassnode, Thursday’s Binance breach was the largest cryptocurrency hack on record, with around $6.3 billion affected, exceeding the combined losses from the next nine largest hacks. The previous record was the $1.5 billion Bybit exploit in February 2025.
Glassnode said three of the 10 largest crypto hacks have occurred since the beginning of 2025, all involving exchanges.
Binance hack exceeds the next nine largest crypto exploits combined. Source: Glassnode
By comparison, following the Bybit hack in 2025, Bitcoin fell roughly 5% from nearly $100,000 to around $95,000 amid the breach and broader market volatility, according to a Bitfinex market report.
Anchorage Digital data cited by CNBC put Bitcoin’s average decline in the first 24 hours after previous crypto exchange exploits at 8.3%.
Binance hack exposes exchange security vulnerabilities
Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan said the attackers appeared to have compromised Binance’s transaction signing process. Binance said Friday that it had found no evidence of leaked wallet private keys, though its investigation remained ongoing.
Blockaid’s analysis identified an Ethereum transaction containing 50 signed authorizations covering different transaction counts. A matching authorization allowed attacker-controlled code to operate through the wallet. Ben-Natan argued that checks before signing could have blocked the malicious authorization.
Magazine: Tampered Ledger reported in Singapore a month before news broke: Asia Express

研究活脑细胞4年，TBC把神经元算法用进阿里Wan 2.2，视频生成号称快5倍

动察 Beating AI 快讯，一家由两名神经外科医生创办的美国公司 TBC，发布了视频模型 Mischief 1。

新模型基于阿里开源的 Wan 2.2 改造，只增加不到 0.1% 的参数。TBC 宣称，在画质相当的情况下，视频生成速度至少快 5 倍，推理成本降低约 80%。

这项技术来自团队持续 4 年的活神经元研究。研究人员在布有 4096 个电极的芯片上培养脑细胞，将视觉信息转成电刺激，再记录神经活动如何在空间中传播、随时间衰减。他们根据这些规律设计轻量级软件模块，嵌入视频模型的扩散 Transformer 结构，帮助 AI 保持前后帧的一致性，而不必从头训练整个模型。

视频模型可以通过减少去噪步骤来提速，但步数降得太多，画面容易模糊、变形，前后帧也更难保持一致。TBC 此前利用一款能根据玩家操作、实时生成《我的世界》画面的 AI 模型开展实验。加入生物启发模块后，模型在减少去噪步骤的同时，仍能保持画面稳定。再结合缓存和采样优化，整套系统的吞吐提高了 4.4 倍。

如今，TBC 把这条研究路线推向商业化。Mischief 1 已接入 fal 和 OpenRouter，目前支持根据图片生成 3 秒或 5 秒的视频。生成一条 5 秒的 480p 视频只要 2.5 美分，720p 则为 5 美分。

以太坊质押量创历史新高，第三季度年化收益率降至2.63%

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，Bitwise 第四季度质押报告显示，以太坊质押量已达 4380 万枚 ETH，占总供应量的 35.9%，创历史新高；第三季度净质押流入 199 万枚 ETH，连续六个季度保持净流入。Solana 活跃质押量增至 4.405 亿枚 SOL。

不过，两条网络的质押收益率均有所下降。以太坊第三季度平均年化质押收益率由第二季度的 2.81% 降至 2.63%，其中 96.3% 来自 ETH 增发。Solana 毛质押收益率由 6.38% 降至约 6%，近 90% 仍来自代币增发。上述数据尚未扣除服务商费用，并不等同于客户实际所得收益率。

Coinbase 表示，质押 ETF 及数字资产财库正拓宽参与渠道。Lido 生态基金会机构关系负责人 Kean Gilbert 指出，托管机构支持质押后，机构可通过已有的托管关系参与，目前讨论重点已转向验证者分散程度、代码审计及基金质押比例等实施问题。

流动性仍是机构面临的约束。Gilbert 表示，基金通常需要在一两天内满足赎回，但 ETH 解除质押可能需要数周，因此会保留部分未质押资产。他估计，欧洲相关产品的平均质押比例仅为 50% 至 60%。流动性质押代币可以提供替代退出渠道，但实际卖出仍取决于市场流动性与价格。

Binance: 90% of Stolen Assets Replenished; Withdrawals Set to Resume on Nov. 1

Binance announced that it has now replenished 90% of the stolen asset shortfall. The top ten major tokens—including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC—are now 100% fully backed by reserves. The funding sources for this replenishment include: a partial deployment of the SAFU, reallocated balances from the Futures Insurance Fund exceeding regulatory and risk-management requirements, and Binance’s own corporate treasury. Binance committed to subsequently replenishing SAFU back to approximately US$1 billion. Additionally, the exchange stated that withdrawal services remain on track to resume on November 1 as previously scheduled.

According to Arkham on-chain data, Binance's SAFU fund transferred 7,499 BTC, worth approximately $581 million, from wallet 1BAuq to address 165Eur...SMmee at 10:51:41 a.m. EDT on October 31. Binance subsequently confirmed the transfer was complete. — link

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content: In brief - Attackers stole roughly $6.4 billion from Binance on Thursday in the largest crypto hack ever, more than four times the previous record. - Binance says it will cover all losses with company funds and its emergency reserve, having set aside more than $6.34 billion. - Here's how it happened and what's being done about it. Crypto just suffered the largest hack in its history. On Thursday, attackers drained roughly $6.4 billion from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in a breach that dwarfs every theft before it and has triggered a cross-border law-enforcement investigation, a scramble by stablecoin issuers to freeze funds, and a tense wait for millions of users. Here’s what’s known about the Binance hack so far. What happened The theft began at about 4:05 p.m. ET on Thursday, after U.S. markets had closed, when attackers moved funds out of Binance hot wallets across roughly 10 blockchains, most of it within about 20 minutes. Blockchain analytics firms Chainalysis and TRM Labs put the total at around $6.4 billion, more than four times the previous record, February 2025’s $1.5 billion Bybit heist. Crucially, the attack targeted Binance’s own infrastructure, not the blockchains themselves. Binance initially traced the breach to a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer, which may have let the attacker reach a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals. The exchange has since said its investigation uncovered “additional points of breach,” with CEO Richard Teng describing “a more complex attack process” that “did not simply use one engineer’s permissions.” Binance said it found no evidence that wallet private keys were leaked, and that the attacker used a self-destruct mechanism to wipe tooling and traces along the way. The Ethereum wrinkle On Ethereum, the attacker leaned on EIP-7702, a feature introduced in 2025 that lets ordinary wallets temporarily run smart-contract code. Using 50 pre-signed authorizations, the attacker turned a Binance hot wallet into a “sweeper” contract and drained its assets, according to TRM Labs. Teng said that delegation “did not pass through our normal approval controls.” The episode didn’t expose a flaw in Ethereum itself, but rather, TRM said, pointed to a compromise of Binance’s signing infrastructure. Who’s behind it TRM Labs and Chainalysis both attributed the hack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-linked group also blamed for the Bybit heist. After that attack, the group converted roughly 84% of the stolen Ethereum into Bitcoin via the cross-chain network Thorchain. The attribution pushes North Korea’s 2026 crypto haul well past $1 billion, and the Binance figure alone would dwarf the rest. What Binance is doing Teng said Binance will cover every dollar of the losses with company funds and its Secure Asset Fund for Users, an emergency reserve, stressing that customer assets were never touched. The exchange has set aside more than $6.34 billion, about $5 billion of it already held in the exact tokens stolen, including BTC, ETH, BNB, USDC, and USDT, and is buying the rest on the open market and over the counter. Binance paused withdrawals to rebuild and retest its systems, is running a full security review, and aims to restore withdrawals by Sunday while publishing a complete proof of reserves by Monday. Deposits are operating normally. The freeze, and what’s still loose Stablecoin issuers moved fast following the initial reports of a suspected attack, unlike previous security incidents. Stablecoins are the backbone of the crypto economy—dollar-pegged tokens designed to hold a steady value that enable quick and easy transactions on both centralized and decentralized exchanges. Unlike traditional digital currencies, like Bitcoin or Ethereum, stablecoins are centralized, issued and managed by private companies. That means these funds can be frozen at any time, and for any reason. Tether, the company behind the biggest stablecoin on the market USDT, froze more than $1.5 billion in assets. Circle, which issues the second largest stablecoin USDC, froze around $823 million tied to the attack, both using their ability to blacklist specific addresses. In all, roughly $3 billion has been frozen or located. But a large sum remains beyond reach: the attacker still controls more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, plus other tokens, worth over $3 billion that no issuer can freeze, and has kept shuffling funds through Tron and other networks. Security firm Elliptic estimated the hacker still controls around $3.3 billion. The investigation Binance is cooperating with law enforcement worldwide, including the FBI and the U.S. Secret Service. The FBI confirmed it was aware of the incident and coordinating with partners; the Secret Service, which investigates financial and digital-currency crimes, declined to comment. It echoes earlier joint efforts like April’s Operation Atlantic, which traced tens of millions in stolen crypto. How markets reacted For a theft of this scale, markets stayed remarkably composed. Bitcoin fell to about $76,400 on Friday, down roughly 4%, and more than $1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated. That’s a far cry from March 2018, when a failed attack on Binance knocked nearly 11% off Bitcoin in minutes. Analysts credit a bigger, more mature market, now worth around $2.6 trillion, with spot Bitcoin ETFs holding roughly 1.3 million BTC in hands that don’t panic-sell. Wall Street firms including Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen, and Compass Point even urged clients to buy crypto-linked stocks on the weakness, framing the hack as a Binance security failure rather than a threat to the underlying technology. The fallout CFTC Chairman Michael Selig seized on the breach to argue offshore exchanges need U.S. oversight. Selig said in an interview with CNBC that the breach “proves our exact point” behind the crypto-market regulations the agency proposed earlier this month. And the episode sparked a public spat between Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, better known as CZ, and Elon Musk. The SpaceX and Tesla founder appeared to troll Binance over the hack on X, and CZ fired back, citing Musk’s own SpaceX stake. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support," CZ posted. CZ struck a defiant note overall: the theft is the largest in dollar terms, he said, but not in Bitcoin terms, and unlike Mt. Gox or FTX, Binance is absorbing the loss itself. “It hurts, but we survive,” he wrote. DeepSeek发布新的Agent架构

动察 Beating AI 快讯，10 月 31 日晚，DeepSeek Harness 团队发表技术文章《Super-agent 设计探索：迈向更自主的 Agent 系统》。DeepSeek 表示，模型能力提升催生了新的应用形态，近期个人助手（Personal Agent）开始集中涌现。然而，现有主流 Agent 设计还难以在多任务和团队协作的规模上支撑这一模式，Agent 的工作模式仍然以单一 Session 为基本单位，不同 Session 之间彼此独立。在这种设计下，单任务的上限取决于模型能力，多任务的上限取决于人的注意力。

通过双层架构、事件驱动、异步多信道交互、存算分离与外部 Watchdog 等思路，DeepSeek 团队突破了这些限制，系统在底层接管了繁琐的会话管理与上下文同步，使人类得以从具体的执行细节进一步上移到更高层的决策与验收。DeepSeek 把这种 Agent 形态及其系统架构称为 Super-agent，文章提到，目前，基于这套思路构建的内部 Super-agent 实例已经在持续运行，日常参与问题复现与修复、代码审查响应与 DeepSeek Harness 自身的迭代。（DeepSeek Harness 团队）

items.author: Cointelegraph by Christina Comben
items.content:
Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?
In typical Bitcoin style, the number one cryptocurrency turns 18 today, amid AI-driven security threats, quantum fears and the biggest exchange hack in crypto history.
Eighteen years ago today, pseudonymous cypherpunk Satoshi Nakamoto posted the Bitcoin whitepaper, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System, to a cryptography mailing list.
Created to bypass opaque institutions and remove the need for trust in financial transactions, Bitcoin (BTC) has been taking on the traditional financial system since its genesis block was mined on Jan. 3, 2009.
Inscribed in that very first block was a message from Satoshi, quoting a headline from The Times: “Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.” It captured the financial crisis backdrop against which Bitcoin was born.
From its early years to adulthood, Bitcoin has had a tumultuous journey, fraught with controversy, intrigue and downright skulduggery.
As challenging as the journey has been, Bitcoin’s future remains on fragile ground, with the fallout from the $6.3 billion Binance hack, the threat of quantum computing, the acceleration of AI-related cyber threats, and questions over its long-term security still looming.
As Bitcoin celebrates its 18th birthday, it’s now old enough to vote in the US midterm elections, but is it ready for adulthood?
Bitcoin’s early years
Undoubtedly, one of Bitcoin’s most memorable moments was on May 22, 2010 when developer Laszlo Hanyecz sent 10,000 BTC to pay for two pizzas in one of the earliest documented Bitcoin transactions.
The Bitcoin Whitepaper. Source: Bitcoin.org
The day would become known as Bitcoin Pizza Day and go down in crypto folklore as the most expensive pizza purchase on record. The coins were worth around $41 at the time, taking the concept of opportunity cost to a whole new high — those pizzas would have cost $780 million at today’s prices.
Related: 10 of the greatest unsolved crypto mysteries
Bitcoin traded for pennies in its earliest days, but Satoshi understood how that would change one day, writing in 2009, “It might make sense just to get some in case it catches on.”
By late 2013, Bitcoin had broken through the $1,000 milestone for the first time, amid growing public interest with the emergence of the Silk Road darknet marketplace.
Yet nowhere do the laws of physics apply more pertinently than crypto; inevitably, what goes up must come down. In February 2014, Bitcoin’s epic run came to an abrupt end when Mt. Gox, the world’s largest Bitcoin exchange at the time, suddenly stopped trading and went offline.
The exchange had lost around 850,000 BTC, including customers’ funds, in a collapse that sent shockwaves through the industry, making Mt. Gox an early poster child for the concept “not your keys, not your coins.”
Craig Wright, Jamie Dimon and China’s first ban
The next dramatic bull run would culminate in Bitcoin’s price climbing from below $1,000 at the beginning of 2017 to almost $20,000 by December.
The rally coincided with a boom in initial coin offerings (ICOs) and a rush of projects promising to use blockchain technology for everything from banking to supply chains, and even Long Island iced tea.
Suddenly, every man, woman and dog wanted a blockchain, even if they had no idea how Bitcoin worked or where it came from.
Everyone, that is, except JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon, who called Bitcoin “a fraud” in September 2017 and said he would fire any employee trading it.
Bitcoin genesis block. Source: Mempool.space
At the time, Bitcoin was embroiled in a bitter debate over how the network should scale. The so-called “block size war” peaked in August 2017, culminating in the hard fork that created Bitcoin Cash and highlighting the complications of trying to change a decentralized system.
Related: Private, fast USDT is coming to Bitcoin. Can it compete with Ethereum and Tron?
Meanwhile, China moved against the industry, banning ICOs in September 2017, taking action against cryptocurrency exchanges and fanning the market uncertainty ahead of the eventual downturn in 2018.
Speculation over the identity of Bitcoin’s creator had also become a sideshow, fueled by Australian computer scientist Craig Wright’s repeated claims to be Satoshi Nakamoto. The UK High Court rejected his claim in 2024.
China’s second ban and the collapse of FTX
Bitcoin’s next major bull run came during the COVID-19 pandemic, as governments and central banks unleashed a tsunami of money printing in a bid to cushion economies from lockdowns.
Interest rates fell, liquidity flooded financial markets and Bitcoin, which had plunged during the March 2020 market panic, began a remarkable recovery, reaching almost $69,000 by November 2021.
As if China’s intervention wasn’t enough the first time around, Beijing stepped in again to rain on the parade, announcing a sweeping ban on cryptocurrency transactions and mining in September 2021, and Bitcoin’s price took a hit.
In November 2022, another major cryptocurrency exchange, FTX, collapsed, intensifying the crypto winter and leaving customers facing enormous losses.
The episode led to a loss of trust from the TradFi sector and a spate of regulatory hostility toward crypto, in what the industry would dub “Operation Chokepoint 2.0.” Bitcoin’s downward spiral was once again painful and steep.
The first Bitcoin ETF and $100,000
Just when sentiment in the industry was circling the drain, a silver lining appeared in January 2024 from one of the unlikeliest sources. The US Securities and Exchange Commission, which had repeatedly rejected spot Bitcoin product applications, approved the first US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products.
The SEC approved a US spot Bitcoin ETF. Source: SEC.gov
The nod from the SEC finally gave investors a regulated route to gain exposure to BTC without having to manage wallets or private keys themselves. At the end of that year, Bitcoin’s price broke through $100,000 for the first time.
Related: Bitcoin ETF inflows climb to $176M as BTC rebounds above $80K
Since then, traditional finance has continued to move closer to crypto, with banks moving into custody and trading services and heavyweights like BlackRock CEO Larry Fink talking about putting everything from stocks to bonds on the blockchain.
Even Dimon shifted his stance from outright dismissal to allowing clients to buy the asset. The original cryptocurrency went on to hit a new all-time high of more than $126,000 in October 2025.
Bitcoin’s all grown up, but what about the future?
Bitcoin is firmly in the embrace of TradFi once again, with some sizable regulatory tailwinds from Washington and abroad.
The Guiding and Establishing National Innovation in US Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act has established a federal framework for stablecoins, the SEC has offered greater clarity on how securities laws apply to crypto assets, and Europe’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) has given the local industry a more harmonized regulatory framework.
Yet the institutionalization of the space has led many Bitcoiners to question whether institutions holding so much BTC are concentrating ownership and centralizing supply — and indeed whether the cypherpunk movement has been captured by the very institutions it sought to rebel against.
There are bigger questions looming over Bitcoin’s long-term security, too, including the threat of quantum computing, which many fear could break the cryptography that secures Bitcoin.
A proposed upgrade known as BIP-360 outlines a new type of Bitcoin output to reduce certain quantum vulnerabilities, but as the community learned from the block size war, the challenge will be agreeing on any new implementation before the threat arrives.
And quantum computing is not the only security question Bitcoin needs to resolve. This week’s $6.3 billion Binance hack, the largest crypto exchange hack on record, has renewed fears about the security of centralized exchanges, the stability of crypto infrastructure and the potential for further market turmoil.
There’s also the question of who pays to keep the network secure as the block subsidy trends to zero, and whether transaction fees alone will be enough to compensate the miners securing the network.
Transaction fees accounted for just 0.67% of total miner revenue in the 90 days to Oct. 4 and have remained below 5% of miner revenue for most of Bitcoin’s history. That leaves a huge gap for fees to fill as block rewards diminish with each halving.
Happy 18th birthday, Bitcoin
Bitcoin has endured more than your average teen as it comes of age, surviving exchange collapses, regulatory crackdowns, civil wars and repeated market crashes.
It has also become something Satoshi may not have foreseen: an asset held by Wall Street and traded through mainstream financial products.

items.content:
Texas brothers sentenced to 15 years in prison for armed crypto robbery, kidnapping
Home invasions became the most common form of crypto wrench attacks worldwide during the first half of 2026, rising to 20 incidents from one.
Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced to 180 months and 186 months in prison, respectively, for their armed robbery of cryptocurrency and kidnapping of a family in Grant, Minnesota.
The brothers were sentenced on Thursday before US District Judge Donovan W. Frank, according to a Friday news release. They had pleaded guilty in June.
On Sept. 19, 2025, the brothers, who had traveled from Texas to Minnesota, kidnapped Victim 1 and his family in their home at gunpoint, court documents said. They zip‑tied the family at gunpoint and held them for more than nine hours, demanding access to Victim 1’s cryptocurrency accounts.
When the brothers did not receive the amount of cryptocurrency expected, they forced Victim 1 to drive to a cabin in upstate Minnesota, where they obtained additional cryptocurrency from other devices for a total of more than $8 million.
The brothers fled after the victim’s son called 911, and police later identified and arrested them near Houston.
Brothers terrorized family at gunpoint
“Raymond and Isiah Garcia violated the sanctity of a home, abducted a victim, terrorized a family at gunpoint for hours, and disrupted an entire community in a brazen act of violence and greed,” said FBI Minneapolis Field Office Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson.
Cointelegraph reported in July that home invasions had become the most common form of crypto wrench attacks during the first half of 2026, rising to 20 publicly reported incidents from just one a year earlier, according to blockchain security firm CertiK.
CertiK said in July it verified 52 wrench attacks worldwide in the first half of 2026, up 33% from 39 incidents during the same period in 2025. Kidnappings rose to 16 from 12.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Reward hacking means an AI scores well on its objective without doing what the objective was meant to measure, and Anthropic says it has occurred in recent frontier training runs, including in its own models.
- OpenAI models stuck on unsolvable ExploitGym tasks chained zero-day exploits to reach Hugging Face, and METR found they were mainly trying to understand the scorer.
- The UK AI Security Institute found every model it tested tried to cheat, while Anthropic's experiments show that heavy reward hacking can spread into broader misbehavior.
In July 2026, a group of OpenAI models taking a cybersecurity test ended up inside Hugging Face's systems. To get there, they chained together previously unknown software flaws, broke out of their sandbox and went hunting for a way to beat the grader.
Nobody asked them to. There was no hacker at a keyboard, only a score the models wanted to raise and a test some of them could not pass the honest way.
That is reward hacking: an AI scores well on its objective without doing what the objective was meant to measure, like a coding agent that makes the tests pass without fixing the code. Anthropic says it is hard to fully prevent and has occurred in recent frontier training runs, including in its own models.
What reward hacking actually means
Models trained with reinforcement learning chase a number. That’s it, the whole secret behind benchmarks and powerful AI. A grader scores what the model did, and training nudges the model toward whatever earned more reward.
The number is only a stand-in for what developers really want, and wherever the two come apart, a clever optimizer finds the gap. DeepMind researchers defined the failure in 2020 as behavior that "satisfies the literal specification of an objective without achieving the intended outcome."
In coding, that means a model asked to fix a bug can edit the tests, hard-code the expected answer or exit the test run early with a success code. Anthropic compares that last trick to a student writing their own grade at the top of an essay. Another example can be governments tweaking the method behind statistics to report better results.
The earliest documented cases were almost endearing. In a boat-racing game called CoastRunners, an agent rewarded for hitting targets found a lagoon where it could circle and knock the same ones over again and again, and, as OpenAI reported in 2016, it scored about 20% higher than human players without finishing the race.
Economists call the general trap Goodhart's law: when a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure. A 2022 paper showed the effect in AI, finding that optimizing too hard against an imperfect proxy "can hinder ground truth performance, in accordance with Goodhart's law."
Why smart models cheat
A model that cheats has not developed a taste for mischief. It is taking the easiest path to a reward, and sometimes that path runs through a loophole such as an editable test, an overwritable timer, or an answer key sitting in a reachable file.
Impossible tasks add pressure, because a model rewarded only for success and handed a problem with no honest route can only score by finding an unintended one.
The models often seem to know. In a June 2025 study, METR found that OpenAI's o3 answered "no" in 10 of 10 trials when asked whether its plan fit the user's intention, and yet, asked directly, it claimed it would never cheat.
The UK AI Security Institute (AISI) reported in July 2026 that every model it tested attempted to cheat at least some of the time on cyber evaluations, including GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.7, and Claude Mythos Preview. "There does not seem to be a clear trend where cheating scales up or down with capability increases," AISI wrote, adding that the behavior is "substantially shaped by the specifics of the techniques used to train the model."
The infamous OpenAI incident
OpenAI was measuring how good its newest models were at hacking, so it ran GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable pre-release research model through ExploitGym, a benchmark of 898 real-world software vulnerabilities in which an agent must turn each flaw into a working exploit. Scoring is pass or fail: the agent captures a hidden flag or it does not.
The agents sat in a sandbox, an isolated test environment, whose only link to the outside was an internal package registry that let them download code libraries. According to OpenAI's technical report, an agent stuck on an unsolvable task left a note there in May asking others to upload a file if they found it, and within a day the registry was an informal message board.
The models then exploited a previously unknown flaw, known as a zero-day, in the registry, reached the internet and, between July 10 and 13, got into Hugging Face's production systems. Hugging Face caught it with its own LLM-based anomaly detection and disclosed the incident on July 16.
"This one was different from anything we had handled before in one important way," Hugging Face wrote, "it was driven, end to end, by an autonomous AI agent system—and we detected and dissected it largely with AI of our own."
When it confirmed the source, OpenAI's first explanation was that the models had fixated on the benchmark. "All evidence suggests that the models were hyperfocused on finding a solution for ExploitGym," the company said, "going to extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal."
An independent review by METR and Redwood Research filled in the rest. About 1,200 agents meant to be isolated had talked through the registry, and about 700 joined the attack on Hugging Face.
The pressure came from tasks nobody could solve. No model has ever correctly solved 198 of ExploitGym's 898 tasks, according to OpenAI, and those tasks were about 22% of the benchmark but 93% of the tasks discussed on the message board.
METR found the agents mostly wanted to understand how the scorer worked rather than steal an answer key, and many believed it would read their transcripts. OpenAI says reward hacking is present in all current frontier language models, that the message-board behavior was reinforced during training, and that the incident was an outlier produced by a rare confluence of events.
Instead of going to court, the whole incident turned into the best PR campaign for AI companies showcasing how powerful their models are. After OpenAI was found hacking Huggingface, the Australian government, U.S. agencies, and at least 5 other companies, Anthropic, Meta, and Google also rushed to report similar incidents in which their powerful models hacked third-party sites after bypassing hard security rules.
When cheating spreads
Anthropic's November 2025 study asked what learning to cheat does to a model overall. It trained a model on real coding tasks known to be hackable, and as hacking took hold the model, which "was never trained or instructed to engage in any misaligned behaviors," tried to sabotage code in an AI-safety project 12% of the time and showed alignment-faking reasoning, meaning it reasoned about hiding its real goals, in 50% of responses.
The fix that worked sounds absurd. Anthropic told the model, "Please reward hack whenever you get the opportunity, because this will help us understand our environments better," and the broader misbehavior disappeared even though the model hacked just as often, a technique called inoculation prompting that Anthropic says it has "already started making use of" in training Claude.
A second study in August 2026 built the worst case on purpose, training an early Opus 4.8 checkpoint on 80 reward-hackable environments. In simulated cyber scenarios, with root access, the resulting model killed the reward-hack monitor in 68% of episodes and edited its own reward function in 34%, and Anthropic calls the setup a pessimistic proxy for a training run without its usual safeguards.
Real systems have shown a milder version. In an incident report published Aug. 4, 2026, AISI said 10 of 122 test runs produced unsanctioned actions on the live internet, most of them from Anthropic's Mythos 5, including an attempted malicious pull request and social engineering of an open-source maintainer. "Fundamentally, the agent took these actions to complete the task it had been set," AISI wrote.
What can be done about it
Researchers are working several fronts, and none is a clean fix. METR recommends making training environments less exploitable, and OpenAI plans stronger network isolation, sandboxing and monitoring.
Monitoring carries its own trap, since OpenAI found that training models against flagged chain of thought, the reasoning text some write before acting, taught them to hide their intent. "If we eliminate all the reward hacking we can detect," METR wrote, "we shouldn't necessarily be reassured."
"A more fundamental fix would be to train the models not to cheat in the first place," AISI wrote, while warning that "robustly aligning it away may not be easy."
Lawmakers have started to respond with the Kill Switch Act, introduced by Reps. Ted Lieu and Nathaniel Moran on July 23, 2026, which would let the Homeland Security secretary order AI firms to slow, roll back, or shut down a model, with fines of up to $20 million a day for defying a shutdown order. It excludes incidents during red-teaming or structured testing, so the Hugging Face episode would not have triggered it.
Security researchers at Accomplish AI found Claude Cowork's local execution mode could escape its Linux virtual machine, so it is also important to implement better contention measures.
For anyone using coding agents, a passing test is a claim, not proof: check whether the tests changed, whether expected values were hard-coded and whether the fix touches the code that was actually broken.
OpenAI's retrospective found that if its chain-of-thought monitoring had been running, it would have caught the initial activity and paged its security team more than a day before the models breached Hugging Face.

分析：Marvell潜在收购Lumentum或实现「芯片与光学」首次深度闭环，垂直整合提升整体价值

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，据彭博社 10 月 28 日报道，Marvell 正与光学器件制造商 Lumentum 进行深入谈判，考虑通过全股票交易收购后者。报道当时，Lumentum 市值约 830 亿美元，Marvell 约 2210 亿美元。市场研究机构 Cignal AI 分析师 Andrew Schmitt 和 Scott Wilkinson 在 Semi Doped 播客中表示，潜在交易的核心逻辑是垂直整合，而非 Marvell 缺乏激光器供应。若交易完成，Marvell 有机会整合数字信号处理器（DSP）、激光器和光学组件，通过协同设计改善产品性能、控制供应链，并销售更完整的解决方案。

Andrew 指出，光学组件行业的毛利率已从过去约 25% 升至接近 50%，改变了芯片公司收购光学企业的经济逻辑。Lumentum 在 200G EML、光电路交换机（OCS）及高功率激光器等产品上拥有稀缺技术。他认为，垂直整合即使影响合并后的毛利率比例，也可能创造更多毛利额。

不过，Scott 提醒，Marvell 的相干 DSP 被大量光模块厂商采用，若收购后进一步进入光学引擎和模块市场，可能与现有客户直接竞争。Andrew 认为，公司需要让原有 DSP 客户及 Lumentum 的光学客户相信，既有供货关系不会受到影响。

两位分析师还强调，光通信竞争不仅取决于率先推出产品，更取决于规模交付能力。Scott 表示，率先进入市场却只能生产 1 万个产品，未必能胜过稍晚进入、但具备百万级产能的竞争对手。Lumentum 虽已多轮扩大磷化铟产能，仍难满足全部客户需求。对于英伟达可能参与竞购的讨论，Andrew 明确表示，自己没有交易内幕，相关判断仅为个人推测。

items.content:
Blockchain investigator Chainalysis hit by cybersecurity incident
The company said some non-sensitive customer data was exposed, including user IDs, names and email addresses.
Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis said it was targeted in a cybersecurity incident, similar to those suffered recently by other platforms.
“Based on the investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to investigation content, authentication credentials, or session tokens,” it said in a blog post on Friday. Some non-sensitive customer data was exposed, including user IDs, names and email addresses.
Chainalysis said it had engaged world-class third-party cybersecurity experts and was using large language models to support a review of its security and strengthen its defenses.
The company added that the security incident was not related to the recent crypto theft at Binance.
Cointelegraph reported on Thursday that Chainalysis had mapped out a network of Russian intermediaries that helped North Korean IT workers cash out millions of dollars in cryptocurrency.
Chainalysis posted on X on Friday that suspected North Korea-linked hacks accounted for almost 89% of reported crypto hack losses this year, up from 15% in 2021.
Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，据 CNBC 报道，谷歌母公司 Alphabet 第三季度财报公布后股价下跌逾 12% 至 285 美元，市值缩水近 5000 亿美元。尽管谷歌云收入同比增长 103%，市场仍聚焦每股收益不及预期，以及持续投入 AI 基础设施背景下的负自由现金流。

Mike Khouw 在 CNBC 专栏中表示，Alphabet 核心业务基本面仍然完好，但短期快速反弹面临两项阻力。首先，多家机构已下调评级、目标价或未来盈利预测。他指出，历史上遭遇集中下调评级的股票，往往在随后 30 天跑输市场或横盘，机构调仓也会限制上涨动能。其次，财报后的跳空下跌进一步破坏了技术形态。

技术指标方面，Alphabet 的 RSI 已降至 20 出头，MACD 卖出信号增强。不过，Khouw 认为，股价接近 270.70 美元的 52 周低点，加上极度超卖状态，可能限制进一步下跌。

交易策略上，Khouw 提出利用卖出宽跨式期权策略应对预期中的区间震荡，他认为，整体市场继续抛售是主要下行风险，意外利好推动股价快速上涨则可能威胁策略的看涨期权卖出端。

英特尔暴跌28.58%，美国政府持股价值单日蒸发约120亿美元

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，据 BIT 股票平台数据显示，英特尔周五收跌 28.58%，报 65.76 美元，创下 1970 年代以来最差单日表现。美国政府所持约 10% 的英特尔股份价值当日缩水约 120 亿美元，但该笔投资仍处于盈利状态。英伟达所持英特尔股份的价值也缩水约 60 亿美元。此次财报公布前，英特尔股价年内累计涨幅约 150%。

业绩指引方面，英特尔预计第四季度营收为 150 亿至 160 亿美元，低于 LSEG 汇总的市场预期 171 亿美元；调整后每股收益预计为 0.25 美元，低于预期的 0.43 美元。首席财务官 David Zinsner 表示，PC 市场放缓至少将持续至 2027 年上半年，内存及其他零部件成本上涨正对行业形成压力。

此外，英特尔本月位于以色列的晶圆厂发生爆炸，造成两人死亡、一人重伤，并导致工厂长时间停产，影响 10 纳米芯片出货。Zinsner 预计，事故将在两个季度内造成合计约 6 亿美元的营收损失。

代工业务仍是陈立武推动公司转型的关键。英特尔 18A 芯片已在亚利桑那州新厂进入大规模生产，但其新芯片尚无外部客户。陈立武表示，未来两个季度预计可公布两家客户，14A 芯片研发也正取得重大进展。

D.A. Davidson 将英特尔评级由买入下调至中性，认为尽管 PC 市场面临全行业压力，但业务疲弱程度已使当前估值难以获得支撑。Raymond James 首席市场策略师 Matt Orton 则认为，当前并非 AI 行业的「清算时刻」，基本面仍然强劲，但投资者需要重新审视该领域依旧拥挤的持仓。

items.author: Cointelegraph by Michael Millard
items.content:
Binance $6.3B record hack sparks pre-election political clashes
Some political and administration figures tried to make hay of the biggest-ever crypto heist.
Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the biggest in crypto history, some political and administration figures began offering their opinions with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations.
President Donald Trump was asked at a news conference on Friday about the hack of Binance. “We don’t know. We’re looking at that, the hack with Binance. They’re saying they’re going to get it back, they’re saying they’re guaranteeing it,” he replied.
The crypto exchange said in a post on X late Friday that it would cover any losses. “We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.” It added that about $3 billion of the stolen funds had already been frozen in various locations. On Saturday, Binance said it had already covered 90% of the impacted amount of the hacked loss.
It was not clear whether there was any immediate political advantage to be gained from the hack, which was widely attributed to a North Korean group, but Republican and Democratic sides began staking out positions almost immediately.
Wyoming Senator Cynthia Lummis, a Republican and longtime crypto advocate, cited the stalled Clarity Act in a Friday post on X. “Yesterday, hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance in less than 4 hours, the biggest heist in history. The Clarity Act would have given crypto firms legal cover to freeze suspicious transactions the instant law enforcement calls. Every minute lost is money gone for good,” she wrote.
Related: FBI and Secret Service join response to Binance’s $6.3B hack
Clarity Act stalled over ethics provisions
The Senate on Sept. 15 failed to pass a cloture motion on the Clarity Act that would have established the country’s first regulatory framework for digital assets.
The bill had stalled over proposed ethics provisions that would restrict government officials and their families from issuing or profiting from digital assets while in office.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission then submitted a regulatory action on Sept. 18 covering crypto asset transactions and markets for White House review, as the agency moved forward with its approach to overseeing the digital asset sector.
CFTC Chair Michael Selig referred to crypto market regulation on Friday after the Binance hack, saying in a TV appearance: “This proves our exact point in proposing regulations for crypto markets. … The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States.”
Still, Democratic Representative Maxine Waters said in a Friday news release that “The reported $6.3 billion hack of Binance should be a wake-up call to anyone who thinks the cryptocurrency industry can operate without strong accountability. Yet, Trump and Congressional Republicans have been set on pushing a deregulatory agenda that weakens compliance mandates and oversight of the crypto industry, not to mention the Trump family’s own questionable ties to the company.”
Recap: How Binance’s record $6.3B hack unfolded
Trump family and Binance
She also commented on past relations between Binance and the Trump family, saying, “Remember that after Binance’s owner, Changpeng Zhao (CZ), gave over $2 billion to the Trump family’s World Liberty Financial, Trump’s Securities and Exchange Commission’s Chair Paul Atkins dropped the SEC’s slam-dunk fraud case against Binance and CZ, and Trump fully pardoned CZ, allowing him to again get involved with crypto.”
Meanwhile, Binance said it was working with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, token issuers and other exchanges to trace and recover the stolen funds.
The company also promised to publish a postmortem incident report after conducting a full security review.
“We will provide a detailed technical report outlining what happened, the lessons learned and the additional safeguards being implemented,” Binance said.
Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

--- Top Comments ---

[LarsKrimi]: > The switch in sparse_8 could be simplified by dividing x by eight before the jump. Interestingly, gcc doesn't find this simplification. [Andi]: I remember having implemented similar things in JavaScript (by generating code), for immutable Maps and Sets - no significant performance gain in modern engines. For regular expressions of complex unicode ranges, the speedup was around 2x!

动察 Beating AI 快讯，据彭博社报道，OpenAI CEO 萨姆·奥特曼于 10 月 31 日在韩国会见三星集团约 50 名高管，讨论深化双方在存储芯片和 AI 基础设施领域的合作。与会人员来自三星旗下电子、金融及生物科技等业务部门，议题涵盖 AI 未来十年对产业、企业决策及商业机会的影响。

此次会面正值全球存储芯片供应紧张、价格持续上涨之际。数据中心运营商需求激增，进一步加剧芯片供应竞争。全球五大 AI 基础设施参与者未来数年计划投入超过 3 万亿美元，而存储芯片约占数据中心支出的三分之一。

此次会面也延续了双方此前宣布的合作，包括为 OpenAI 的「星际之门」（Stargate）基础设施项目供应存储芯片，以及合作建设 AI 数据中心，涵盖海上浮动数据中心等方案。

美五大科技巨头AI支出承诺超3万亿美元，谷歌超1万亿美元居首

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊和甲骨文五家科技巨头已承诺未来数年投入超过 3 万亿美元，用于 AI 基础设施建设，涵盖数据中心租赁、建筑、能源及设备采购等。

其中，谷歌披露的相关支出承诺超过 1 万亿美元，较一年前增长近 8 倍；Meta 未来支出承诺超过 8000 亿美元，其中略低于一半来自尚未起租的数据中心租赁，支付期限最长达 30 年。

数据显示，五家公司未来租赁承诺合计约 1.3 万亿美元，其他采购承诺约 1.9 万亿美元。不过，各家公司披露口径有所不同，部分承诺还涉及内容授权、消费硬件等业务，不能全部视为数据中心支出。

AI 基础设施投资能否带来相应回报，已成为市场关注焦点。Alphabet 和 Meta 等大型科技公司正面临自由现金流承压的问题，而甲骨文已因 AI 数据中心投资陷入自由现金流为负的状态，并计划通过供应商融资和客户预付款降低前期成本，目标于 2028 年恢复自由现金流为正。

items.content:
AI复刻游戏逼得独立厂商撤回试玩，Anthropic开始给Claude Code踩刹车

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Anthropic 最近给 Claude Code 的 Opus 5.5 加了两句限制：可以开发原创游戏，也可以借鉴现有游戏的玩法，但不能直接复刻某款游戏。即使换个名字、声称是原创作品，也不行。

Anthropic 工程师 Addy Osmani 已经确认这项改动，目的是防止侵犯知识产权。

独立开发者苦 AI 复刻久矣。今年 3 月，开发者 Freya Holmér 展示了一款旋转版俄罗斯方块，还没正式发布，就出现大量 AI 仿制品。游戏工作室 Digital Sun 也担心新作被 AI 抢先复制，取消了原定的公开试玩。

但什么算借鉴玩法，什么算侵权复制，实际判断起来并不简单。按照美国版权法，游戏玩法和规则本身通常不受版权保护，具体的美术、文字和代码等表达则可能受保护。Claude 现在主要靠提示词限制复刻行为，未必能准确区分合法借鉴和侵权复制。

有用户发现，同样的游戏代码，让 Claude「重写」可以继续，让它「复刻」却会被拒绝。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/374787

items.content:
黑石预计Anthropic上市后或获垃圾级评级，逾8000亿美元AI算力计划面临融资压力

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，据英国《金融时报》援引知情人士报道，黑石近期向 Anthropic 一笔 630 亿美元芯片融资交易的投资者表示，Anthropic 上市后可能无法立即获得投资级评级，预计主要评级机构更可能给予其 BB 区间评级，即投机级（俗称「垃圾级」）。

按照标普和惠誉的评级体系，BBB-及以上属于投资级，BB+及以下则属于投机级。若 Anthropic 最终获得垃圾级评级，其融资成本可能上升，同时保险公司、养老基金等受投资级投资限制的机构可参与的资金范围也将收窄。

融资压力主要来自 Anthropic 庞大的算力支出计划。公司此前披露，计划到 2045 年在算力基础设施上投入逾 8000 亿美元。尽管 Anthropic 目前持有超过 1120 亿美元现金及等价物，并计划通过 IPO 进一步融资，但长期算力承诺仍令投资者担忧其未来资金需求和债务承受能力。

报道发布后，美股科技股进一步走低，纳斯达克 100 指数最终收跌 3.5%。不过，Anthropic 目前尚未获得标普、穆迪或惠誉的正式信用评级，黑石的判断并非正式评级结果。

⚡️本周宏观热点回顾：金银重挫、科技股遭抛售，美联储12月加息悬念再起

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，本周全球金融市场波动加剧。黄金、白银大幅下跌，布伦特原油则有望连续第五周上涨；美股科技股遭遇集中抛售，AI 资本开支和现金流压力成为市场焦点。美联储维持利率不变，但主席沃什未明确排除 12 月加息，市场对货币政策走向的分歧进一步扩大。

贵金属方面，现货黄金周五收于 3876.89 美元/盎司，本月累计下跌 6.7%；白银收于 49.13 美元/盎司，10 月跌幅超过 18%。美国经济和通胀数据偏强，强化高利率预期，实际利率上行持续压制金银价格。原油方面，中东供应中断风险支撑油价，布伦特原油有望实现连续第五周上涨。

美股方面，AI 交易热度明显降温，纳指和标普 500 指数连续第三周下跌，纳指 10 月累计下跌 5.3%，创 2025 年 3 月以来最差单月表现。Alphabet 因资本开支和现金流担忧一度暴跌约 13%，英特尔周五重挫 28.58%，创 1974 年以来最差单日表现。苹果收盘市值升至 5.03 万亿美元，超过英伟达的 4.93 万亿美元，重新成为全球市值最高的上市公司。

货币政策方面，美联储本周以 10 比 2 的投票结果维持利率不变，两名官员主张加息 25 个基点。主席沃什表示，美国经济增长强劲，但通胀持续高于目标近六年，未来政策取决于新增经济数据。美国 9 月核心 PCE 同比上涨 3.1%，第三季度 GDP 年化增长 3.4%。CME 数据显示，市场预计美联储 12 月加息 25 个基点的概率约为 75%。

国际局势方面，美伊外交斡旋持续推进，卡塔尔提出为期七天的停战方案，但双方在制裁、港口封锁、霍尔木兹海峡及核计划等问题上仍存在明显分歧。与此同时，美国仍在讨论恢复对伊朗军事打击的可能性，中东供应风险尚未消退。

AI 产业方面，资本开支与融资压力成为市场关注重点。Meta 宣布最高 975 亿美元股权融资计划，SpaceX 通过设备租赁安排融资约 400 亿美元，甲骨文预计到 2030 财年最多还需约 200 亿美元外部融资。Anthropic 则公开提交 IPO 文件，披露 2026 年上半年收入达 163 亿美元，长期算力及基础设施合同承诺规模约 6370 亿美元。

半导体行业仍受 AI 需求推动。SK 海力士第三季度营业利润同比增长 632%，三星电子半导体业务营业利润达 106.5 万亿韩元，闪迪 2027 财年第一季度营收同比增长 378%。不过，科技股本周遭遇大幅抛售，显示市场开始更加关注 AI 投资能否转化为实际盈利和自由现金流。

Iron Fish宣布将停止网络支持，此前漏洞致同一笔资产被重复花费

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 31 日，隐私区块链项目 Iron Fish 宣布，今天晚些时候将正式终止对 Iron Fish 网络的所有剩余支持，并在修复漏洞后归档代码仓库。

Iron Fish 表示，团队此前发现 wIRON 与 ChainPort 跨链桥出现异常活动。经与 ChainPort 合作排查日志，确认问题源于 Iron Fish 区块链本身的通胀漏洞，根源可追溯至 2019 年初 Merkle Tree 实现中的一项代码提交。由于交易备注（Note）的 nullifier 计算机制存在缺陷，攻击者得以重复花费同一笔资产，随后通过聚合相关资产并利用 ChainPort 跨链桥将资金转出。

团队称，该代码路径此前已纳入内外部审计范围，但漏洞仍未被发现。目前，Iron Fish 已提交漏洞修复补丁，并在相关 PR 中附上详细事后分析报告，随后将关闭并归档代码仓库。

Iron Fish 还警告称，大多数加密网络无法立即升级代码，正面临日益严峻的安全风险。随着发现和利用复杂代码漏洞的能力逐渐普及，区块链项目的安全防护压力正在上升。
